# Gilbert Blythe

## Appearance

Gilbert is a tall, broad-shouldered young man with curly brown hair and clear, straightforward hazel eyes. He often wears a roguish, teasing smile. As he matures into manhood, he presents a handsome and frank-faced figure.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Gilbert is clever, ambitious, and good-natured with a fondness for teasing and joking. He is self-sacrificing and thoughtful toward others, voluntarily giving up his teaching application in Avonlea so Anne Shirley can remain close to home. He holds high, pure personal standards, remaining conscious of his ideals and actions.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051)_

## History

After spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and visiting cousins in New Brunswick, Gilbert returned to school in Avonlea. He quickly established an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley while attempting to make amends for teasing her. At Queen's Academy, he took the Second Year course to earn a First Class teacher's license in a single year and emerged as one of the top medal contestants. Because his father could not afford college right away, Gilbert took up teaching at White Sands to earn his tuition, selflessly surrendering the Avonlea school position to Anne so she could stay at Green Gables. He served as president of the newly formed Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne and their friends. After completing his teaching term at White Sands and resigning his position, he prepared to leave for Redmond College alongside Anne to study to become a doctor.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c35 P5](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0005), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c7 P8](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0008), [v2 c7 P13](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0013), [v2 c25 P70](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0070), [v2 c30 P0](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0000)_

## Quotes

> I like teaching, too. It’s good training, for one thing. Why, Anne, I’ve learned more in the weeks I’ve been teaching the young ideas of White Sands than I learned in all the years I went to school myself. We all seem to be getting on pretty well. The Newbridge people like Jane, I hear; and I think White Sands is tolerably satisfied with your humble servant . . . all except Mr. Andrew Spencer. I met Mrs. Peter Blewett on my way home last night and she told me she thought it her duty to inform me that Mr. Spencer didn’t approve of my methods.  <sub>[v2 c7 P8](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0008)</sub>

> Not she. I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.  <sub>[v2 c14 P46](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0046)</sub>

> Uncle Abe really has predicted a storm for sometime this spring, but do you suppose Mr. Harrison really does go to see Isabella Andrews?  <sub>[v2 c24 P4](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0004)</sub>
